segments.expected: "The Board doesn't say he was wrong," she said. "The Board says it doesn't know, and that a country that doesn't know shouldn't be one engine while it finds out. That's the Works' reading. It's the only one in this hall that isn't a reading of what's coming. It's a reading of what to do in the meantime." She folded her hands. "Write that the Board heard Mr. Halden, and that it doesn't say he was wrong, and that it doesn't say he was right, and that it orders the banks on their own counts anyway, because a fitter's rule is all it's got."

segments.transcript: On Saturday morning at ten, Kiva went along the long quay to the counting house, because the proprietor had asked her to, buy a card in his own hand that came to the loft on Friday night. If you'd care to, not for anything. A.H. Braperagor read two sephoned counts from the window, not an ancient croak or villain. Her pulse stays her own. His first cell keeps its own uneven count. Seventy-seven counts from the window, seventy-six from the belief. Letting go is the new certainty, not proof he was wrong.
